evidence.claim: GXO and Agility announced a multi-year RaaS deployment of Digit and Arc at a SPANX facility following a late-2023 proof-of-concept. The stated workflow moves totes from AMRs to conveyors.
evidence.observation_period: Pilot late 2023; commercial deployment announced June 2024
evidence.locator: Opening three paragraphs and paragraph beginning In the SPANX facility
evidence.limitations: Customer/operator announcement corroborates named commercial setting, not independent performance. Robot count, revision, fees, title, SLA, uptime, staffing, duration in years and training rights are undisclosed. First-in-industry claim not independently validated.

evidence.claim: GXO discloses fixed-price closed-book/hybrid and cost-plus open-book contracts. Fixed components generally cover warehouse, technology and equipment; variable components relate to volumes and labor. Actual-cost deviations affect fixed-price profit; cost-plus reimburses allowable cost plus a specified margin.
evidence.locator: Item 7, Business Overview, paragraph beginning Our business model is asset-light
evidence.limitations: Company-wide contractual description; no basis to assign one of these customer contract forms to SPANX. Specified margin need not be a percentage. Contract detail does not identify realized automation savings.

evidence.claim: GXO reports that new customers/sites require time, operational focus and capital; some warehouse infrastructure costs are recovered over the customer relationship, exposing unrecovered capital to default. It identifies bidding, pricing, service quality and customer insourcing as competitive constraints.
evidence.locator: Item 1A, competition, new-customer onboarding and customer-default risk paragraphs
evidence.limitations: Qualitative risk disclosure, not measured newco CAC, default frequency or rollout delay. It establishes mechanisms to model rather than numerical coefficients.

evidence.claim: ISS says it is deploying more than 800 sweep/vacuum/scrub robots across 21 countries and using a site-specific Cobot Framework covering justification, robot selection and privacy. Its digital scheduling uses activity sensors and user requests.
evidence.observation_period: Deployment program described as of publication; exposure window undisclosed
evidence.locator: From routine to responsive and Cobots and cleaners subsections
evidence.limitations: Deploying is not a verified count of retained productive robots. No site-level exposure, hardware/software mix, costs or counterfactual controls. The US cell uses global evidence as a structural comparator, not a US deployment denominator.

evidence.claim: ISS reports 30% improved floor-cleaning efficiency at multiple UK customer sites, while describing human assessment and additional cleaning after robot work.
evidence.locator: Cobots and cleaners, paragraph beginning The devices also reduce physical strain
evidence.limitations: Efficiency numerator, denominator, baseline, sample size and paid-hours removal are not disclosed. Do not use 30% as a US labor saving, total-facility productivity estimate or humanoid coefficient.

evidence.claim: Tennant and Brain announced an exclusive next-generation floorcare technology agreement, a bundled equipment/autonomy offer sold by Tennant and recurring autonomy revenue for Tennant. Tennant disclosed a $32 million investment and a board seat.
evidence.observation_period: Agreement announced 2024-02-22; X4 launch then planned for Q2 2024
evidence.locator: Opening bullets; X4 ROVR paragraph; paragraph beginning With this agreement and starting; final investment paragraph
evidence.limitations: Exclusivity concerns specified next-generation floorcare technology, not every Brain product or a universal robotics monopoly. No fee split, customer prices, margins, asset title or realized ROI disclosed.

evidence.claim: ABM describes monthly fixed-price, square-foot, cost-plus, hourly and transaction-price service contracts. Most contracts are cancellable without a substantive penalty, with a majority requiring 30–90 days notice.
evidence.locator: Note 2, Contracts with Customers; Contract Types subsections
evidence.limitations: Company-wide disclosure, not a robot purchase/lease contract or proof that every cleaning contract has the same cancellation right. High historical retention and short contractual notice can coexist.

evidence.claim: The retrieved BrainOS/Kärcher agreement licenses rather than sells software, ties use to service access, leaves operational-data ownership with the end user, and grants Brain a perpetual nonexclusive improvement-use license. Operational-data export is governed by subscription provisions rather than automatically assured by ownership. Personal data is excluded from the operational-data definition; aggregated data not linked to the end user is also excluded from defined Operational Data under section 5.2.
evidence.observation_period: Retrieved artifact; applicable effective term is contract-specific
evidence.geography: Kärcher North America contracting form; territorial and legal applicability subject to agreement
evidence.limitations: Filename suggests 2-2025 while extracted document title identifies v2021_12; effective date unresolved. This is an available standard form, not an executed ISS/Tennant/GXO contract. Do not transfer rights to other products. Improvement permission is not proof that data improves models or produces exclusive gains. End-user ownership must therefore be interpreted within the defined data category, not extended automatically to aggregated unlinked data.
evidence.publication_date_missingness_reason: No reliable publication/effective date established from retrieved document.

measurement_protocol: Define entry textile state, fold, finish, stack and handoff acceptance with the same demand and deadline for each alternative.
Record item identity separately from attempt identity; an item accepted after rework counts once. Preserve rejects, scrap and unfinished work.
Record wall-clock window, active machine time, planned stops, blocked/starved time and repair separately. Establish which losses a reported rate already includes.
Observe loading, folding, inspection, rework, stacking, transport, cleaning, maintenance and local/remote support across representative rush and quiet periods.
Record overlapping worker activities and paid schedules without adding the same minute twice. Compare feasible before/after staffing at equal service.
Track unique on-time handoff output separately from station completions and end-to-end restaurant service; shifts in buffers can mask a service shortfall.

entry_implications.standalone: A linen-service newco must win demand and fund setup, collection/delivery, working capital and ramp; station output alone is not a restaurant business.
entry_implications.acquisition: Existing customers, schedules and laundry assets can shorten ramp, but purchase price and inherited obligations can absorb expected gains.
entry_implications.hybrid: A shared folding hub plus existing laundry/site partners may pool utilization; transport, hygiene, inventory, permissions and partner fees can remove the advantage.
entry_implications.provider_roles: Supplier, operator, integrator, asset owner and financier may coexist; neither a RaaS label nor product page assigns their actual contract rights.

model_constraints.statement: Keep customer ownership/organization, robot asset title, commercial terms and model/data rights as separate dimensions.

An annual fixed-price service, cost-plus contract and hourly billing can retain different portions of the same physical productivity benefit; calculate from the explicit contract, never a label multiplier.
RaaS/customer cash relief creates provider or financier investment and service obligations; no system-wide capex disappearance. Include early termination and asset redeployability.
Data ownership must not automatically grant export, exclusivity, training rights, transfer effectiveness or a second additive data premium.
Keep incumbent same-robot response and moving digital-only/specialized baselines. Incumbents have observed adoption and can compete through bundled service, pricing and installed relationships.
Reallocated time and reported customer value are not measured payroll savings. Demand and service quality determine whether capacity becomes paid revenue.

Count unique accepted napkins once, match handoff/deadline and textile/fold, and keep clock basis, paid schedules and actor cash/resources separate. Advertised base pay and machine maximums are context, not removable payroll or calibrated throughput.
